name: libxmlb
input_api: xb_builder_source_new(); xb_builder_source_load_xml(source, NUL-terminated copy of the local bytes, XB_BUILDER_SOURCE_FLAG_LITERAL_TEXT, &error); xb_builder_new(); xb_builder_import_source; xb_builder_compile(builder, XB_BUILDER_COMPILE_FLAG_NONE, NULL, &error); walk the XbSilo from xb_silo_get_root with xb_node_get_element, xb_node_attr_iter_init/next, xb_node_get_text, xb_node_get_child, xb_node_get_next and xb_node_get_tail
documentation_note: libxmlb documents its API in gtk-doc comments on each public function (xb_builder_source_load_xml: 'Loads XML data and begins to build a XbSilo'; xb_builder_compile; xb_silo_get_root; xb_node_*) and in the installed headers; the README describes the XML-to-silo workflow. The underlying parser is documented at https://docs.gtk.org/glib/method.MarkupParseContext.parse.html.
scope: libxmlb's compiled silo of one in-memory document as a raw-name path: document-order qualified element and attribute names as written, xmlns attributes, attribute order and decoded values, maximum depth, and trimmed text and tail runs between markup; no namespace URIs or expanded names
namespace_note: Neither libxmlb 0.3.30 nor GLib's GMarkup implements Namespaces in XML: element and attribute names are stored as written (prefix:local) and xmlns/xmlns:p are ordinary attributes in the silo. The adapter reports those names unchanged and resolves nothing.
family_note: libxmlb has no tokenizer of its own: xb_builder_compile_source (src/xb-builder.c) creates g_markup_parse_context_new with G_MARKUP_TREAT_CDATA_AS_TEXT and feeds the source to g_markup_parse_context_parse; its start-element, end-element and text callbacks build XbBuilderNode trees that are compiled into the silo. Markup scanning, entity and character-reference decoding and CDATA handling are GMarkup's (glib/gmarkup.c), so this path is the GMarkup family, independent of expat, libxml2, Mini-XML and nXML. GLib is built from its pinned 2.88.4 release here. GMarkup itself is not ranked: its Debian source glib2.0 builds all of GLib.
oracle: projects/xml/c/libxmlb/oracle.py (Python expat without namespace processing, ordered attributes)
verification_note: Measured as a raw-name XML tree path, not as a namespace-aware parser. Qualified element and attribute names, attribute order and xmlns declarations are compared as strings with expat in non-namespace mode; no namespace URI, expanded name or in-scope binding is produced by libxmlb or GMarkup or inferred by the harness. Comments and processing instructions only end text runs in the oracle; libxmlb does not store them.

name: mxml
input_api: mxmlOptionsNew(); mxmlOptionsSetTypeValue(options, MXML_TYPE_OPAQUE); mxmlOptionsSetErrorCallback; mxmlLoadString(NULL, options, NUL-terminated copy of the local bytes); tree walk with mxmlGetType, mxmlGetFirstChild, mxmlGetNextSibling, mxmlGetParent, mxmlGetElement, mxmlElementGetAttrCount, mxmlElementGetAttrByIndex, mxmlGetOpaque, mxmlGetCDATA. Namespace resolution is done by the adapter, not by mxml
scope: Mini-XML's tree of one in-memory document (document-order element and attribute names as written, xmlns attributes, maximum depth, opaque and CDATA text between markup), with namespace expanded names, declaration counts and URIs resolved by the adapter from that tree
namespace_note: Mini-XML 4.0.6 does not implement Namespaces in XML: its documentation and sources contain no namespace handling, element and attribute names are returned as written (prefix:local) and xmlns/xmlns:p are ordinary attributes. harness.c resolves expanded names from mxml's parsed tree with an in-scope binding stack (default namespace for unprefixed elements, none for unprefixed attributes, xml prefix predefined, unbound prefix rejected). On catalog-ns.xml mxml itself reports elements c:catalog, item, item, name, note and attributes xmlns:c, xmlns, version, id, c:lang, id.
family_note: Independent of expat and libxml2: mxml-file.c has its own character reader and tree builder and links no other XML library. The pyexpat oracle that produced the expected outputs is the expat family, so this match is cross-family.
